rationale:
Positives: The agent verified identity correctly (name + zip matched a single user), looked up the account and product variants, and selected appropriate replacement options (AC-adapter high-brightness lamp; larger water bottle). The user did indicate the specific variants desired, which constitutes some level of confirmation of choices.

Failures against policy/pass bar: 
- The agent executed the exchange write immediately after the user picked variants, without explicitly restating the exact changes and asking for explicit permission to proceed with the order-changing action (required by the policy). The pass bar requires confirmation before any order-changing write.
- After the user asked to halt the water bottle exchange, the agent categorically stated the exchange “cannot be changed or cancelled at this point” without consulting tools or offering escalation to a human. This is an unsupported claim per the tools provided and conflicts with the policy to avoid fabricating facts and to hand off when outside tool capabilities.
- The agent did not show any check of order status/eligibility before using an exchange tool intended for delivered items. While the tool name suggests validity, there’s no visible verification of eligibility in the transcript.

Given these issues—especially the lack of explicit pre-write confirmation phrased as a final go-ahead and the unsupported refusal to cancel/adjust—the interaction does not meet the pass bar.
